summary: Magalloway Mountain lookout: first tower 1910, current tower and wood cab 1935, cab airlifted in 2006; in service; sources disagree on the elevation.

facts.design: Standard New Hampshire wood cab on the tower built in 1935 (register)

access.note: Reached on foot. Magalloway Road is a gravel logging road; just over five miles in, a narrower and rougher road branches off and dead-ends three miles later at the trailheads, passable in a passenger car if driven slowly. The register links to a rental flyer for the cabin, which could not be opened. Whether the tower cab is open to visitors is not documented.

visit.trail_note: Up the Bobcat Trail, a visit to the Overlook, then down the Coot Trail: about two miles total

facts.agency: NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development

events.note: First lookout put into service, funded by the NH Timberland Owners Association (called the Timberline Owners Association in one article)
State forestry report for 1915-1916 says a new and improved watch tower was constructed; it does not say which earlier tower it replaced
Forestry report for 1921-22 lists a new cabin and a telephone extension to the tower
Current tower with a standard NH wood cab was built, replacing the second of two wooden towers on the site; the register calls it the last wood tower in the state
Coos County fire lookout stations, including Magalloway Mountain, were closed the week of October 9, 1937 (Portsmouth Herald, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page); no reason given
Registered March 12, 2002; nominated by Chris Haartz
A new tower cab was airlifted to the tower on August 4, 2006
July 2009 vandalism: cabin and storage shed trashed, an attempt to break into the tower cab, more than $1,000 in damage
NHLR visit report dated June 16, 2010: staffing recorded as sometimes; directions to the tower recorded as signed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 3,360 ft (1,024 m) for the lookout and the hiking article gives 3,383 feet for the summit. The record keeps the register figure, which matches elevation_m in the brief; the story reports both.

The register names the 1910 funders as the Timberland Owners Association; the hiking article writes Timberline Owners Association. These look like the same group with two spellings, and the story says so.

notes_for_editor: Current status and access are unverified after 2010. The NHLR rental link points at nhdfl.org, which did not resolve, and the NH state reservations page returned 403, so rental terms are unconfirmed. Sources 2 and 3 are secondary (a hobbyist site quoting newspapers; a hiking article with no date visible in the cache). The 1937 closure and 2009 vandalism are known only from the Forest Lookouts page. Brief record's access 'unknown' can be set to public for the trail; the cab's visitor status stays open.
